subject: Entitlement escrow reconciliation for Q3 Dedicated GPU commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@opentide.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Entitlement escrow reconciliation for Q3 Dedicated GPU commitments

Sara —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the signed MSA. We reviewed the Q3 commitments this morning and theres a shortfall in available dedicated capacity across the cluster during the 3–8pm US-PST window that overlaps several customers (including Opentide). Before we escalate formally, I want to propose a pragmatic escrow + prioritization approach so we can honor contractual SLAs while minimizing disruption.

Proposal (high level):
- Create an entitlement escrow for Opentide equal to 80% of the committed baseline for Q3 while we finalize capacity expansion (estimated 6 weeks).
- Apply a short-term prioritized routing policy: live traffic -> escrowed slots -> best-effort burst (preemptible).
- Offer a one-time credit if we need to preempt >5% of Opentide production tokens in July.

Next steps: Can Lauren/Monica confirm whether Opentide will accept escrowed allocation + credit, and can Dylan validate whether we can operationalize the routing policy without rolling restarts?

Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: Q3_commit_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with committed v. available capacity)

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@opentide.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: opentide-sales@opentide.ai
Date: 2027-07-11T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement escrow reconciliation for Q3 Dedicated GPU commitments

Ben —

Appreciate the heads-up. The signed MSA (attached) was explicit about baseline entitlements and monthly minimums. Opentide cannot accept a permanent downgrade of baseline capacity. Were open to a temporary escrow if: 1) you commit to a firm timeline for restoring full baseline, and 2) the credit covers customer impact and our internal SLA penalties.

To be concrete: if escrow reduces our production ability by more than 10% during peak hours we will need a 15% credit or equivalent capacity guarantee elsewhere. Were also evaluating a parallel failover to Stratus for a subset of traffic; can you confirm whether youve engaged them on cross-cloud bursting?

Sara Kim
Head of Platform, Opentide AI
sara.kim@opentide.ai

Looping ops in. Quick operational notes:
- We can create an escrowed entitlement bucket and enforce it at the routing layer with a weighted policy within 2 business days. No rolling restarts required; policy can be attached to route config.
- Short-term capacity expansion (adding 24xA100 equivalent) is estimated at 4–6 weeks depending on quota and procurement.
- For immediate mitigations we can enable a cross-tenant burst queue that uses lower-priority preemptible nodes; thats a stopgap only.

Dylan: can you validate whether cross-cloud bursting with Stratus is feasible from a networking/security posture (wed need an E2E encrypted tunnel + IRM controls)? If not, we should propose the credit.

Im attaching an ops mitigation plan with the policy knobs Im proposing.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@opentide.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement escrow reconciliation for Q3 Dedicated GPU commitments

Sara —

Thanks for the clarity. From a commercial perspective we want to avoid churn — Opentide is strategic and the deal (OP-4372) unlocks reserved capacity economics. Id propose this compromise:

1) Entitlement escrow at 85% of committed baseline for up to 6 weeks.
2) If preemption >5% occurs in any billing week, Redwood issues a 12% credit against that weeks usage (applies only to preempted capacity).
3) Redwood commits to a capacity roadmap milestone (procurement PO placed by 2027-07-20; capacity online no later than 2027-08-26).

If Opentide accepts those three items we can mark this as an agreed mitigation and avoid engaging legal on an amendment. Sara — can you confirm acceptance on behalf of Opentide by EOB Tuesday PST?

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: Q3_commit_matrix.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@opentide.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-14T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement escrow reconciliation for Q3 Dedicated GPU commitments

Sara —

Following internal ops validation and Monicas commercial compromise, were prepared to move forward as follows (final summary):

- Entitlement escrow: 85% baseline (effective immediately)
- Credit: 12% applied to any billing week where preemption of entitlements >5%
- Capacity roadmap: procurement PO to be issued by 2027-07-20; projected online date 2027-08-26
- Cross-cloud bursting: Ops will continue exploring Stratus; no dependency on that for the escrow agreement

Please reply to this thread with a short confirmation so we can operationalize the routing policy and update billing. If you prefer, I can ask Legal to convert into a short amendment, but Monica and I both think the credit + PO timeline should suffice as a commercial patch.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
